name: Damien Black

tenures.source: Wins the federation's own eight-man tournament final at its debut pay-per-view (28 September 2003) to become the first champion; appears on every card through 28 October 2003.

caption: The federation's first World Heavyweight Champion, crowned in an eight-man tournament at the promotion's debut pay-per-view and still holding the belt when the surviving record ends.

identity.note: A different wrestler billed under the same ring name is recorded in another wing's own material; nothing in either record links the two.

name: Evan Crowley

tenures.source: Reaches the final of the debut tournament (28 September 2003) and later wins, then loses, the federation's Intercontinental Championship by 26 October 2003, when a back injury takes him off the following card.

caption: A top contender who fell short of the federation's first two world title opportunities and lost the Intercontinental Championship at Redemption before a back injury sidelined him.

name: Jimbo

tenures.source: Loses on the 16 September 2003 weekly show, then wins a first-round tournament match and reaches the second round at the 28 September 2003 debut pay-per-view.

caption: An early-card tournament entrant who won his opening bout before falling in the second round of the federation's first title tournament.

identity.note: A different wrestler billed under the same ring name is recorded in another wing's own material; nothing in either record links the two.

name: Damien Omega

tenures.source: Loses a first-round tournament match at the 28 September 2003 debut pay-per-view, loses again on 21 October 2003, then wins the federation's first tag team match on 26 October 2003.

caption: A tournament-era competitor who found his first win in the federation's own inaugural tag team match.

name: The Freak

tenures.source: Wins on the 16 September 2003 weekly show, advances through the 28 September 2003 tournament on a disqualification, loses on 30 September 2003, and wins again at Redemption on 26 October 2003.

caption: A recurring undercard wrestler who advanced through the federation's first title tournament and later won at its second pay-per-view.

name: Titanium

tenures.source: Appears on every card read this pass between the 16 September 2003 weekly show and the 28 October 2003 weekly show, without a recorded singles win.

caption: A frequent undercard opponent across the federation's first two months who is not recorded winning a match in the surviving record.

identity.note: A different wrestler billed under the same ring name is recorded in another wing's own material; nothing in either record links the two.

name: George Lamere

tenures.source: Wrestles on the 16 September 2003 weekly show, the 28 September 2003 debut pay-per-view, the 30 September 2003 weekly show, and the 26 October 2003 pay-per-view, without a recorded win.

caption: A large, hard-hitting wrestler billed as a giant who fought in some of the federation's most violent matches, including a Hell in a Cell bout, without a recorded win.

name: Danielle

tenures.source: Accompanies Damien Black to the ring at the 28 September 2003 debut pay-per-view and is struck from behind by an opposing wrestler during the 30 September 2003 weekly show.

caption: Damien Black's on-screen girlfriend and ringside companion, targeted by his rivals to get at him.

name: Paul Valentine

tenures.source: Billed as a self-proclaimed legend and "Crippler" Evan Crowley's cornerman from the debut pay-per-view (28 September 2003) onward; wrestles Damien Black himself on 30 September 2003 and later ambushes Johnny Lambert on 28 October 2003.

caption: "Crippler" Evan Crowley's cornerman and a wrestler in his own right, willing to interfere directly whenever his allies needed it.

identity.note: A different wrestler of the same name is recorded in another wing's own material; nothing in either record links the two.

name: The Shit

tenures.source: Loses at the 28 September 2003 debut pay-per-view, draws on 30 September 2003, assaults an opponent backstage on 21 October 2003, wins a Hell in a Cell match on 26 October 2003, and loses an Intercontinental Championship match on 28 October 2003.

caption: A masked-then-unmasked giant whose feuds ran hottest inside a Hell in a Cell before he came up short in his own bid for the Intercontinental Championship.

name: Tommy Starr

tenures.source: Wins a Fans Bring the Weapons match at the debut pay-per-view (28 September 2003) before losing by disqualification later that night; wins the vacant-in-effect Intercontinental Championship at Redemption on 26 October 2003 and retains it on 28 October 2003.

caption: A hardcore-style fan favorite who became the federation's first Intercontinental Champion and retained the title through the end of the surviving record.

identity.note: Other wrestlers billed under the identical name are recorded elsewhere in the museum; nothing in any record links them.

name: Total Control

tenures.source: Draws on the 16 September 2003 weekly show, loses a Fans Bring the Weapons match on 28 September 2003, loses again on 30 September 2003, and loses on 28 October 2003.

caption: An undercard heel wrestler who never won a recorded match across the federation's first two and a half months.

name: DLC4Life

tenures.source: Wrestles the opening match of the 16 September 2003 weekly show, ruled a draw after outside interference.

caption: A one-time opponent from the federation's own first weekly show, billed from Amsterdam.

name: Mayhem

tenures.source: Wrestles under the ring name "The Luv Machine" on 30 September 2003, is renamed "Mayhem" by 21 October 2003, wrestles in the federation's first tag team match on 26 October 2003, and wins again on 28 October 2003.

caption: A wrestler who won his early matches as "The Luv Machine" before adopting the ring name Mayhem and feuding with Titanium and Brian Karagias.

identity.note: Other wrestlers billed under the identical name are recorded elsewhere in the museum; nothing in any record links them.

name: Brian Karagias

tenures.source: Debuts under the ring name "Rampage" on 30 September 2003, wrestles under his own name from 21 October 2003, wins the federation's first tag team match on 26 October 2003, and ambushes an opponent before losing by disqualification on 28 October 2003.

caption: A debuting wrestler who arrived under the ring name Rampage before wrestling under his own name and feuding with Mayhem and Titanium.

name: Simon Poole

tenures.source: Loses on 21 October 2003 and again, after an opponent's ringside ally interferes on his behalf, at Redemption on 26 October 2003.

caption: A wrestler billed as "The New F'N Diamond" who lost both of his recorded matches despite outside help.

name: Johnny Lambert

tenures.source: Wins on 21 October 2003, loses a non-title submission match to the World Heavyweight Champion at Redemption on 26 October 2003, and is ambushed before his rescheduled rematch could start on 28 October 2003.

caption: A rising wrestler billed as "The #1 Stunna" whose bid against the World Heavyweight Champion twice ended in interference.

name: Gunta

tenures.source: Loses by submission on 21 October 2003; the broadcast names a promotion-imposed deadline for him to make an impression or be released.

caption: A wrestler given an on-air deadline to prove himself after a quick submission loss.

name: Renegade

tenures.source: Runs in to decide a tag team match on 26 October 2003, then loses a match of his own on 28 October 2003 after an opponent's ally interfered.

caption: A newcomer who first appeared as an interfering ally before wrestling in his own right.

identity.note: Other wrestlers billed under the identical name are recorded elsewhere in the museum; nothing in any record links them.

name: Daniella Dragmire

tenures.source: Accompanies Simon Poole to the ring for the opening match at Redemption, 26 October 2003.

caption: Simon Poole's ringside manager at the federation's second pay-per-view.

name: G-Money

tenures.source: Named as Damien Black's manager, absent from ringside, at Redemption on 26 October 2003; appears in Black's own ring gear as a decoy during an ambush on 28 October 2003.

caption: Damien Black's manager, named in absentia before standing in as a decoy for him during a backstage ambush.

name: Ryan Blasier

tenures.source: Wins his only recorded match on 28 October 2003.

caption: A wrestler billed as "The Reason" who won his sole recorded appearance.

name: Johnny

tenures.source: Calls every card read this pass from the 16 September 2003 weekly show through the 28 October 2003 weekly show.

caption: One half of the federation's regular broadcast team.

name: Felix

tenures.source: Calls every card read this pass from the 16 September 2003 weekly show through the 28 October 2003 weekly show.

caption: One half of the federation's regular broadcast team.

name: Lucas

tenures.source: Announces the federation's own founding on 14 August 2003 and appears on-screen as its president at the 28 September 2003 debut pay-per-view, the 30 September 2003 weekly show, and the 21 October 2003 weekly show.

caption: The federation's founder and on-screen president, who books its matches and occasionally steps into the broadcast booth himself.
